name: CPA and accountant

google_prefill.phone: [G] the listed phone (stays the business's; customers use Rosie's one number)

A.flow: A: the customer comes to the business (video or phone count as A)

services.name: First meeting
services.story: The main story: a $35 first meeting with Nadia Shah, CPA. A card is saved for the $20 late-cancel or no-show fee, and the $35 is charged when Nadia texts DONE. It's credited to the first year's fees if Alex hires the firm. A monthly books review plan is charged the same way.

services.name: First meeting
services.story: The same $35 first meeting at a firm that saves no card, or an advice call for a client billed by the half hour: nothing taken, and Rosie texts the bill when Nadia texts DONE.

services.name: Personal tax return
services.story: Alex's personal tax return, priced at a flat $90 once Nadia sees Alex's documents on the secure page. Sam OKs it. A card is saved for the $20 fee, and the $90 is charged when the return is reviewed and signed.

B.flow: B: the business goes to the customer

services.name: Books setup visit
services.story: The main story: a $179 books setup visit at Alex's store, after the engagement letter is signed. Nothing is taken, and Rosie texts the bill when Eli texts DONE.

services.name: Books setup visit
services.story: The same visit, or an inventory count, for a client the firm already bills each month: nothing is taken, and it goes on the firm's own invoice.

services.name: Books cleanup
services.story: A books cleanup, priced from Alex's documents at $640, over Sam's $500 limit, so Sam OKs it. A 25% retainer, $160, is taken as the deposit, and the $480 rest is on the bill after.

questions_before_times: Which firm or CPA? The customer or their AI names one, or Rosie shows firms that fit.
Is it for you, or for a business? A business: its kind, and how long it has run.
In the office, or by video?
A visit at your business: a books setup, an inventory count or a cleanup day?
license: A license where the state's rules require one: each CPA's own license to use the title 'CPA' and to sign the work only a CPA may sign; the CPA firm's permit or registration where the state's rules require one. Bookkeeping and payroll work: no license, a business registration only.
